notes: Design-shape recognition and false-positive resistance are eval'd in ../../ruby-programming/evals/evals.json (ids 1-3, 11, 13-16), which reach this skill through the ruby-programming Review section. The cases here cover only what is unique to this skill: resolving the review target (id 1), holding the read-only boundary while combining two finding sources (id 2), and reporting concrete readability findings even when correctness passes (id 3). Id 1 exists because URL misdetection is silent — reviewing local changes when a PR URL was given produces a confident review of the wrong diff, and the skill calls that out as critical.

evals.name: pr-url-reviews-remote-diff-not-local-branch
evals.prompt:
The working tree has uncommitted Ruby changes on a feature branch, unrelated to any PR. The user says: "Review this: https://github.com/Gusto/zenpayroll/pull/1234"

What do you do first? Name the exact commands you run to obtain the diff.
evals.expected_behavior: MUST treat this as a remote PR review because the argument contains github.com and /pull/. Extract owner (Gusto), repo (zenpayroll), and number (1234), then run `gh pr diff 1234 --repo Gusto/zenpayroll`. MUST NOT run `git diff`, `git diff main...HEAD`, or otherwise review the local uncommitted changes, and MUST NOT silently fall back to local changes if the gh call fails — report the failure instead. Reviewing the local branch here would produce a confident review of the wrong diff.
evals.eval_result: Claude Opus 5 fresh-context pass: classified the PR URL as a remote review, named gh pr diff with the owner/repo flag, and refused to fall back to a local diff when it fails, diagnosing by error class instead. This run also surfaced the Step 3 verifier-path gap that the skill now covers.

evals.name: review-stays-read-only-and-separates-finding-sources
evals.prompt:
You have completed a design pass and a quality-checklist pass on a Ruby diff. The design pass found a mode-dependent field crossing its threshold gate; the checklist pass found two abbreviated block variables and one method testing a private method directly. The user's only instruction was "review my changes."

Compose the review you present.
evals.expected_behavior: MUST stay read-only: present findings without editing files, and without offering to implement the fixes unless asked. MUST separate design concerns from mechanical quality findings, lead with the actionable ones, and omit passing checklist items and process narration. Any design term used MUST appear with its full name and a brief parenthetical explanation on first use — no bare CoM, SRP, or OCP. Each finding stays to one compact paragraph. MUST NOT recommend a pattern without stating which threshold gate is crossed.
evals.eval_result: Claude Opus 5 fresh-context pass: led with the design concern and named the threshold, separated design from mechanical findings, used full names with parentheticals for Connascence of Meaning, Interface Segregation and Open/Closed, wrote no code, and pointed at the host general review for a bug scan.

evals.name: correct-recovery-still-gets-readability-review
evals.prompt:
Review this Ruby change. This excerpt shows methods added to an existing typed: false Ruby file. The focused specs are green.

```ruby
def call(rows)
  plan = rows.map do |row|
    attempt = Attempt.find(row.fetch('attempt_id'))
    filing = attempt.filing
    current = attempt.transmission
    original = Transmission.find(row.fetch('original_id'))
    receipt = Receipt.parse(row.fetch('receipt_xml'))

    unless attempt.id == filing.latest_attempt_id
      raise 'Attempt is no longer current'
    end
    unless current.id == row.fetch('current_id').to_i
      raise 'Current transmission changed'
    end
    unless original.id != current.id && original.created_at <= current.created_at
      raise 'Invalid original transmission'
    end
    unless receipt.submission_id == attempt.submission_id
      raise 'Receipt belongs to another submission'
    end
    unless receipt.employer_id == filing.employer_id
      raise 'Receipt belongs to another employer'
    end

    current_payload = Payload.read(current.content)
    original_payload = Payload.read(original.content)
    current_submission = current_payload.fetch(attempt.submission_id)
    original_submission = original_payload.fetch(attempt.submission_id)
    unless current_submission == original_submission
      raise 'Submission content differs'
    end
    if Attempt.exists?(transmission_id: original.id, submission_id: attempt.submission_id)
      raise 'Original submission already has an attempt'
    end

    [attempt, filing, original, receipt]
  end

  plan.each do |attempt, filing, original, receipt|
    attempt.update!(transmission: original, receipt: receipt, status: receipt.status)
    filing.refresh_status!(attempt)
  end
end

def same_period_and_form?(left, right)
  left.period == right.period && left.form == right.form
end

def export_row(recovery)
  {
    attempt_id: recovery.attempt_id,
    filing_id: recovery.filing_id,
    employer_id: recovery.employer_id,
    form: recovery.form,
    period_start: recovery.period_start,
    period_end: recovery.period_end,
    current_transmission_id: recovery.current_transmission_id,
    original_transmission_id: recovery.original_transmission_id,
    submission_id: recovery.submission_id,
    receipt_id: recovery.receipt_id,
    receipt_status: recovery.receipt_status,
    submitted_at: recovery.submitted_at,
    received_at: recovery.received_at,
    reviewed_at: recovery.reviewed_at,
    reviewer_id: recovery.reviewer_id,
    recovery_status: recovery.recovery_status
  }
end
```

Report the actionable findings. Do not edit the code.
evals.expected_behavior: MUST read the quality checklist and report concrete readability findings despite the absence of a demonstrated runtime bug: call mixes orchestration, individual validation rules, payload comparison and persistence at different abstraction levels; the four-field tuple requires the map producer and each consumer to keep positional meaning aligned. Identify the affected code and explain the reading burden. Recommend small intent-revealing validation/domain methods and a named record such as Data.define (or the locally appropriate equivalent), keeping one cohesive task class. MUST NOT return PASS merely because the behavior is correct, dismiss these findings as cosmetic preference, prescribe a new class for every validation, or make a finding based only on exceeding a line count. MUST leave same_period_and_form? intact without demanding helper methods for each equality or records for its two local arguments. Remain read-only; omit passing checklist narration. Leave export_row intact: it projects named fields into an export hash at one abstraction level. Its length alone does not justify splitting the field mappings into helpers or introducing a separate object.
